text:
Mookie Betts says Dodgers’ postseason seeding is not a major concern
LAX Leader
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts played down the importance of postseason seeding after the team’s loss to the Braves, according to an Aug. 26 report. The Dodgers are currently competing with the Atlanta Braves and Milwaukee Brewers for one of the top two seeds in their league, which would secure a bye in the Wild Card round.
As of Wednesday, Los Angeles trails Milwaukee by one game and holds second place, four games ahead of Atlanta. The team lost the first game of its series against Atlanta, missing an opportunity to tie with Milwaukee for first place. The next two games have become crucial as they aim to secure a bye from playing in the Wild Card round.
The Wild Card round is structured as a three-game series between two teams, introducing additional risk due to baseball’s unpredictable nature. While fans may prefer avoiding this extra challenge, recent playoff history shows that seeding has not always determined success for Los Angeles.
After Tuesday’s loss to Atlanta, Betts was asked if playoff seeding matters for a team aiming for its third consecutive title. “We’ve won through the Wild Card series. We’ve won with the bye, so I don’t think it really matters,” Betts said. “I mean, if you want to make it matter, sure, but I mean, it doesn’t matter when you play. You’re going to have to get timely hits and pitch, so there’s no secret or magic formula to it. It’s just about playing good ball.”
Last season, Los Angeles advanced past Cincinnati in the Wild Card before defeating Philadelphia in the Division Series and Milwaukee in the Championship Series. Despite being one of baseball's oldest teams this year and potentially benefiting from extra rest provided by a first-round bye, Betts maintained that performance on the field outweighs any strategic advantage from seeding.
